title: Scenario
description: Tool-agnostic definition of a single A/B test: one variable, two variants, exactly one primary KPI and at least one guardrail. Deliberately independent of any testing platform's own schema — whoever imports it maps it to their tool. Several of CLAUDE.md's binding rules are enforced here structurally rather than in prose: rule 2 (one primary KPI), rule 3 (a guardrail exists), rule 4 (one variable, two variants), rule 8 (source is stated), rule 10 (evidence level is stated).

boxItem.description: One bullet in one of the three boxes. The object form carries a bold label; the string form is a plain line.

title.description: The scenario's question. Archive convention is an actual question ending in '?' — a title that asserts an answer prejudges the test.

stage.description: Journey stage / archive file this belongs to, e.g. cart-checkout

rationale.description: Why this is worth testing, in prose. Becomes the card's description.

source.description: Rule 8: a scenario lifted from the archive and one produced for this page must be distinguishable.

variable.description: Rule 4: the ONE thing that differs between the variants. A value naming two things ('renk ve metin') is a rule-4 violation the schema cannot catch — scenario-critic does.

hypothesis.description: A hypothesis states a mechanism, not just a prediction. 'B will convert better' is a guess; 'B converts better because the coupon field stops sending code-less users off-site' is testable.

mechanism.description: The causal clause: why the change should move the metric.

market.description: Rule 11: market is separate from language. null means unknown — which is honest, and blocks carrying one market's result to another.

variants.description: Exactly two. A third variant is a different test design and this schema deliberately refuses to express it.

is_current.description: Rule 15: when the user shared a real page, variant A is that page as-is. Mark it true rather than quietly redesigning the control.

kpis.description: Rule 2 and rule 3, enforced structurally: exactly one primary, at least one guardrail.

evidence.description: Rule 10: the strength of the evidence behind the proposal is always stated. A weak level is allowed; hiding it is not.

sample.description: Rule 5: no duration or sample promise without known traffic. Leave the numeric fields out rather than estimating them.

history.description: Rule 16: what .abtest-history.md says about this variable on this page.

card.description: Optional visual layer consumed by scripts/build_card.py. Absent when the scenario is only being exported, not rendered.
